pr.title: Add comprehensive email validation for blocked users

raw_findings.body: match_count is incremented twice (and the record saved twice) for a single signup attempt, inflating the block/hit statistics that last_match_at and match_count are meant to record.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Statistics data becomes wrong because the side effect runs more times than there are logical signup events.
raw_findings.impact: match_count is incremented twice (and the record saved twice) for a single signup attempt, inflating the block/hit statistics that last_match_at and match_count are meant to record.
raw_findings.root_cause: A read-style predicate method was given a persistent side effect (increment + save) that fires once per validation run.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Do not perform writes inside the predicate; separate the statistics update from should_block?, or update counters once at a single well-defined point (e.g. only when the record is actually persisted / signup rejected) rather than on every validation pass.
raw_findings.title: should_block? mutates and persists on every call, double-counting match_count per signup
raw_findings.trigger: A signup whose email exists in blocked_emails. UsersController#create calls user.valid? (users_controller.rb:168) and then user.save (users_controller.rb:172); each triggers EmailValidator#validate_each which calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value).

raw_findings.body: Read-modify-write race causes one increment to be overwritten, so match_count under-counts the actual number of blocked matches.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent execution loses increments, corrupting the counter.
raw_findings.impact: Read-modify-write race causes one increment to be overwritten, so match_count under-counts the actual number of blocked matches.
raw_findings.root_cause: Counter is updated with a non-atomic load/increment/save sequence.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use an atomic database update such as BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...') instead of loading, mutating in Ruby, and saving.
raw_findings.title: Non-atomic match_count increment allows lost updates under concurrent signups
raw_findings.trigger: Two concurrent signup requests validating the same blocked email at the same time each read match_count, add 1 in Ruby, and save.

raw_findings.body: Regressions in the moved email_domains_whitelist/blacklist handling (e.g. the domain-escaping regexp in email_in_restriction_setting?) would not be caught by this new validator spec.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Review quality fails because moved logic ships without direct test coverage.
raw_findings.impact: Regressions in the moved email_domains_whitelist/blacklist handling (e.g. the domain-escaping regexp in email_in_restriction_setting?) would not be caught by this new validator spec.
raw_findings.root_cause: Behavior was relocated into a new class without migrating/adding tests for its non-blocked branches.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add contexts to email_validator_spec.rb exercising email_domains_whitelist (allowed vs disallowed domain) and email_domains_blacklist (matching vs non-matching domain) to cover the branches now owned by EmailValidator.
raw_findings.title: EmailValidator spec omits coverage of whitelist/blacklist branches it now owns
raw_findings.trigger: The whitelist (email_domains_whitelist) and blacklist (email_domains_blacklist) logic was moved from User#email_validator into EmailValidator#validate_each, but the only spec context added covers the blocked-email path.

raw_findings.body: Rejected emails accumulated in one controller instance would leak into other instances, causing stale email rejections to persist across contexts.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Shared mutable state produces cross-instance contamination of rejected emails.
raw_findings.impact: Rejected emails accumulated in one controller instance would leak into other instances, causing stale email rejections to persist across contexts.
raw_findings.root_cause: A mutable array default was placed on the class prototype instead of being initialized per instance.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Initialize the array per-instance, e.g. set this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A()) inside an init() hook rather than as a shared property default.
raw_findings.title: rejectedEmails declared as a shared Em.A on the class definition
raw_findings.trigger: An array literal declared directly in an Ember class extend is created once and shared by every instance; if more than one CreateAccountController instance is ever created, pushObject on one mutates the array seen by all.

finding.verifier_reason: The patch introduces `should_block?` with side effects (increment + save) at lines 14-16. The repository context shows `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (line 168) and then `user.save` (line 172), each triggering validations. `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, so the counter increments twice per signup attempt. This is a real data integrity issue introduced by the patch.

finding.title: Non-atomic match_count increment allows lost updates under concurrent signups
finding.trigger: Two concurrent signup requests validating the same blocked email at the same time each read match_count, add 1 in Ruby, and save.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch introduces a non-atomic read-modify-write pattern at lines 14-16: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save`. Concurrent requests validating the same blocked email can read the same value, increment in Ruby, and save, causing lost updates. This is a distinct issue from candidate 0 (double-counting vs race condition) with a different fix (atomic update vs moving side effect).

finding.body: Rejected emails accumulated in one controller instance would leak into other instances, causing stale email rejections to persist across contexts.
finding.failure_mode: Shared mutable state produces cross-instance contamination of rejected emails.
finding.impact: Rejected emails accumulated in one controller instance would leak into other instances, causing stale email rejections to persist across contexts.
finding.root_cause: A mutable array default was placed on the class prototype instead of being initialized per instance.
finding.suggested_fix: Initialize the array per-instance, e.g. set this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A()) inside an init() hook rather than as a shared property default.
finding.title: rejectedEmails declared as a shared Em.A on the class definition
finding.trigger: An array literal declared directly in an Ember class extend is created once and shared by every instance; if more than one CreateAccountController instance is ever created, pushObject on one mutates the array seen by all.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch adds `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` at line 17 as a class-level property. In Ember Classic, array/object literals in `extend()` are shared across all instances. If multiple CreateAccountController instances exist, they share the same array. This is a known Ember anti-pattern causing cross-instance state leakage.
